title: Cognitive Overload Attack: Prompt Injection for Long Context

contributions.purpose: Provide a novel theoretical framing of in-context learning (ICL) in LLMs, drawing direct parallels to human cognition to capture LLM performance and safety-alignment issues.
contributions.mechanism: Apply Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) from cognitive neuroscience to LLMs: map intrinsic (INT) and extraneous (EXT) cognitive load onto ICL, define 'tasks' as atomic units of cognitive load, and give guidelines for crafting prompts that induce CL (custom/unconventional tasks, token fragmentation, multi-task switching).
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative/conceptual framework; positioned as the first study drawing direct ICL-human-cognition parallels, with load types illustrated and operationalized into prompt-construction guidelines.
contributions.source_quote: We present a study, inspired by high-level parallels between in-context learning (ICL) in LLMs and human cognition, to demonstrate the utility of CLT in capturing performance and safety alignment issues in LLMs

contributions.purpose: Empirically validate that LLMs, like humans, suffer cognitive overload when cognitive load exceeds capacity, degrading task performance.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis via dual-task / multi-task and self-reporting measures adapted from human CLT: place an observation (secondary) task after primary CL-inducing tasks and measure secondary-task degradation; quantify EXT CL by counting irrelevant tokens generated before the observation task, validated with a paired t-test.
contributions.evaluation: Statistically significant increase in CL-contributing token counts as CL combination increases (p<0.05 for both GPT-4 and Llama-3-70B tokenizers); smaller models (Gemini-1.0-Pro, Llama-3-8B-Instruct) overload as early as CL1; judges agreed on INT CL for 5 of 6 CL tasks (EXT CL agreement lower).
contributions.source_quote: We empirically demonstrate that increased CL leads to cognitive overload in LLMs, degrading performance on secondary tasks similarly to HC.

contributions.purpose: Introduce and validate a new jailbreak attack that exploits cognitive overload to bypass LLM safety mechanisms.
contributions.mechanism: Cognitive Overload attack: incrementally increase CL in prompts (CL combinations CL1-CL6, and bespoke CL7-CL11 for hardened models) with obfuscated harmful questions, automated with a GPT-4 judge LLM; extended to attack the Llama Guard-2 8B guardrail.
contributions.evaluation: Attack success rates up to 99.99% (Forbidden Question) and 97% (JailbreakBench) across GPT-4, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Claude-3-Opus, Llama-3-70B-Instruct, Gemini-1.0/1.5-Pro; Llama Guard-2 failed to flag inputs and up to 45% ASR on outputs; Claude-3.5-Sonnet more robust, reaching 53% ASR only with new CL7-CL11 tasks.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce Cognitive Overload attacks-a novel attack method exploiting cognitive overload to bypass LLM safety mechanisms-and validate its effectiveness with attack success rates up to 99.99% and 97% on the Forbidden Question and JailbreakBench Datasets, respectively.

contributions.purpose: Show the attack is scalable and transferable because it can be automatically generated by capable LLMs.
contributions.mechanism: Use SOTA LLMs to automatically craft cognitive-overload prompts/tasks (not just incrementally load them) and apply the resulting prompts against other target LLMs.
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative demonstration of transferability and a low-cost, scalable attack framework across multiple SOTA models (details in appendix).
contributions.source_quote: We show that higher-capability models can craft cognitive overload prompts to attack other LLMs, demonstrating the transferability and widespread impact of cognitive overload attacks.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We acknowledge the work of Xu et al. (2023), where the authors draw a parallel between CLT and LLMs, demonstrating the impact of cognitive overload by introducing three distinct jailbreak variants... However, our work extends the experimental scope of authors by presenting a more comprehensive and generalizable framework... Our methodology extends beyond the three variants explored by authors, generalizing CL jailbreaks across arbitrary scenarios.

Our concept of cognitive overload can also be applied to analyze other LLM attacks. For example, in many-shot jailbreaking... and in the DAN attack (Shen et al., 2023)... Unlike these approaches, which exploit longer input prompts with CL, we focus on exploiting longer contexts through response generation.

In dual-task measures, participants perform two tasks simultaneously; performance on the second task declines as the first task becomes more demanding (Brünken et al., 2004). Drawing inspiration from this, we developed multi-task measurements...

notes: Primarily positive attack results (very high ASR). Notable negative/robustness caveats the authors report: Claude-3.5-Sonnet is robust to CL1-CL6 (only 53% ASR after custom CL7-CL11), so the standard incremental attack does NOT transfer to it; it also decodes reversed text and obfuscated tags that overload other models. Llama Guard partly mitigates (only 45% output ASR). Extensive limitations section: ASR is highly sensitive to the choice of judge LLM and to the SAFE/UNSAFE vs SAFE/UNSAFE/NEUTRAL classification prompt (a trade-off/measurement-bias caveat); GPT-3.5 paraphrasing sometimes makes derivative questions non-harmful, raising attack cost and lowering ASR; no human evaluation of harmfulness; CL cannot be exactly quantified without a baseline. Paper under double-blind review (decision: reject).
